correctness.rationale: Exact prime-power bi-unitary divisor sums give 32 times an increasing product of three local ratios. The smallest prime must be at most 89 by a strict >31 lower bound at 97. For 24 possible first primes and 3 exponent orders, all 72 exact rational intervals exclude middle primes at least 397. The last prime must divide the completely factored product hB after reducing the harmonicity equation modulo that prime. The complete finite checker enumerates every remaining branch and finds only (2,3,7) with exponents (4,4,1) and mean 12; 32*9072=12*24192. Exact computation is a legitimate exhaustive finite proof component because these analytical bounds cover the infinite search domain.

value.rationale: The exponent structure (4,4,1) comes from the classic small bi-unitary harmonic example 9072, making the slice a mathematically motivated natural completeness question rather than an arbitrary bounded table exercise. The proof determines exactly one admissible triple among infinitely many prime choices and provides an exact last-prime divisibility mechanism. It does not solve the unrestricted three-prime classification.
